title: Patient-Friendly SCI Glossary
source_document: English Master Data Collection & Clinical Content Repository

content.definition: Damage to the spinal cord that affects nerve signals between the brain and the body.
Standardized clinical scale used by medical professionals to measure sensory and motor function after SCI.
A serious medical reaction to discomfort below the injury level in people with SCI at T6 or above.
A blood clot that forms in a deep vein, usually in the leg.
Changes in bladder or bowel control caused by interrupted nerve signals.
A temporary drop in blood pressure when sitting up or standing.
Therapy focused on building skills and adaptations for daily activities and self-care.
Therapy focused on movement, strength, balance, and transfer mobility.
Exercises that move joints through their full natural movement to prevent stiffness.
Involuntary muscle tightness or spasms resulting from changes in nerve pathways.
An infection in any part of the urinary system requiring clinical evaluation.
